title: introduce-adaptive-log-gating-and-token-budget-estimator
author: Maya Thompson
commits: 9a1b3f2: introduce TokenBudgetEstimator core and configuration schema
f4c8d5e: add adaptive log gating middleware and tracing annotations
2b7a9c1: dashboard panel for token budget vs spend (compact view)
c3f7e88: alerting policy and mute-window integration
a7b2d33: add unit + integration tests and CI tweaks
description:
Motivation: Long-running production incidents showed noisy logs and high-cost tail invocations where token cost spikes correlate with unbounded logging. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a TokenBudgetEstimator that predicts per-invocation token budget (expected tokens + safety margin) using light-weight features (model, route, historical prompt shape) and (2) an adaptive log-gating middleware that uses the estimator at request time to decide logging fidelity and span enrichment. The goals are: reduce observability noise for low-value heavy invocations, preserve high-fidelity traces for risky/expensive invocations, and expose token-budget-derived metrics for dashboards and alerting.

What this changes (summary): adds a new estimator implementation (observability/metrics/token_budget_estimator.py) with a pluggable config, adds a tracing/log-gate integration (observability/tracing/log_gate.py) that tags spans with budget_decision and gated_fields, a compact dashboard (console/dashboards/token_budget_overview.json) showing predicted budget vs actual token spend, and new alert rules (alerting/policies/budget_alerts.yaml) to surface cases where actual > predicted * 1.5 for high-SLA tenants. There are docs explaining configuration knobs and rollout plan (docs/observability/token-budget.md). Tests included cover estimator calibration and gating heuristics.

Implementation notes and constraints: the estimator is intentionally conservative and runs synchronously in the request pre-hook with a bounded CPU budget; model pedigrees (model family + tokenization scheme) are considered to keep predictions stable across quantized variants. The gating middleware currently supports two levels: minimal (error + span id) and full (token deltas + KV samples). Gating decisions are emitted as a metric token_budget.gate_rate{decision=minimal|full} for monitoring and can be toggled per-tenant via helm values (deploy/helm/values-observability.yaml).

Rollout plan: behind feature flag (ff_observe_token_budget) and default-off for enterprise tenants. Staged rollout: 1) internal Canary (1% traffic) for 48h with token_budget.gate_rate SLO checks, 2) expand to all internal tenants (7 days), 3) optional customer opt-in. Alerts: added budget overrun alert (SEV3) and gate-rate drift alert (SEV4) with automated quiet-windowing for known maintenance windows.

Risks and mitigations: wrong budget calibration could over-suppress valuable logs; mitigated by conservative multiplier and retaining full logs when spans show error states or when cost > 3x predicted. We also emit a debug telemetry stream (sampled) of gated events for offline QA. Performance: estimator adds ~150us median latency on our canary (measured in local perf bench). Load tests included in this PR run showed <1% p50 latency increase at 99th percentile load for the canary configuration.

release_notes: Introduce TokenBudgetEstimator and adaptive log gating middleware. Adds dashboard panel for predicted vs actual token spend, and alerting for budget overruns. Default-off feature flag; staged rollout plan included.
